Real-time price information empowers vegetable farmers
item.description:
Thanks to mobile phones, rural vegetable growers now know the price of their produce in city markets. Farmers and small traders at the northern trading hub of Mohasthan, Bogra, say that they now come to the market with a realistic idea of prices.
Information about the prices of commodities flows freely thanks to mobile phones. Producers say this has enhanced their bargaining power though the prices ultimately depend on supply and demand.
Studies cited in development literature suggest that mobile connectivity significantly reduces the cost of searching for information. Vegetable growers now often use voice calls and SMS services to contact buyers before harvesting.
Md Aminul Islam (36), a farmer of Rahmotbala village in Bogra Sadar upazila, has grown radish, gourd, pumpkin and yard-long bean on one acre of land. On 2 October, he brought radish to Mohasthan vegetable market. "I knew the price of each maund (40 kilograms) was about Tk 1,000 three days ago, but today it has fallen to Tk 500-600 per maund. This is because of higher supply, and because the quality of this vegetable is sometimes not good when grown in hot weather,” he explained. "Farmers cannot unite to fix the price. Farmers and traders have mobile phones, so both can get information about supply and demand.”
Rabbi Molla (25), hailing from Utholi, Shibganj, who cultivated an early variety of cauliflower on about 50 decimals of land, said they get an idea of the likely prices of vegetables before harvesting by talking to other farmers and traders. "I sold some cauliflowers from the field. I come here (to Mohasthan) hoping for a higher price. Prices go up, prices go down. When the demand for vegetables in Dhaka or other cities increases, that is when wholesalers and traders offer us better prices," he pointed out.
Reading the price situation, many paikars (traders) buy seasonal vegetables from farmers and sell them to Mohasthan-based arotdars (wholesalers) who sell commodities in bulk to their counterparts in Dhaka and other cities. One such trader, Masum Islam (27) of Bichok, Shibganj, said, "I bought bitter gourd for Tk 1,600 per maund from farmers today, expecting to sell at Tk 1,800. I am struggling to get it because we don't know the exact price in advance," he said.
Wholesalers at Mohasthan buy vegetables depending on orders from wholesalers in cities, and also depending on the supply. Cucumbers, auburgines, sponge gourds, pumpkins, yard-long beans and olive are abundant at present. "The higher the supply, the higher the profitability for us. But when there is higher demand in Dhaka, the farmers also ask higher prices. Everybody keeps track of demand and supply, via phone or Facebook. Farmers now get a share of any price-hike," said Abdul Hamid Pramanik (48) of Lahiripara, Bogra, who has been operating in the wholesale market for about a decade.
The Mohasthan trading hub supplies vegetables to different cities. About 200 traders and 70 wholesalers (owners of trading houses) operate here. Al-Mamun (40) is the owner of one such arot (trading house). Maisha Traders. He observed that the use of mobile phones by farmers and small traders has revolutionized farming, ensuring farmers a fair price. "This has increased the competition in the business. You no longer see a huge difference between the price paid at the farm and the wholesale price. Of course any price-hike affects consumers, but farmers benefit," he added.
Hefzul Bari Fakir (40), a representative of Bishal Bhandar wholesale trading house in Mirpur, Dhaka, was at Mohasthan. He said, "I get orders with the likely price from Dhaka via mobile phone. I buy vegetables from farmers and small traders and transport them to Dhaka. Farmers have access to market information, and try to sell to whoever offers them a better price. If production falls, or if there is a problem in communication, vegetable prices go up."
Vegetables are perishable and spoil quickly. Experts have estimated that 30% of the vegetables harvested spoil before reaching consumers. As farmers and traders are now able to get price information quickly, this should help them to sell their vegetables quickly. It is hoped that this will reduce spoilage.

item.title: 4 members of a family from Jessore still missing after Cox’s Bazar resort fire
item.description:
Four members of a family from Jessore have remained missing following the fire at Tuptup Resto & Resort in Ukhiya of Cox’s Bazar on Saturday.
The missing family members are Nahidur Rahman, 41, son of Matiar Rahman of Mohonpur village under Manirampur Municipality in Jashore; his wife, Afsana Matin Tanji, 36; and their two children, Ruzaina Inaya, 7, and Sunaina Ihana, 3.
Family sources said Nahidur worked at an organization called Grand Power Limited in Shyamoli, Dhaka. He used to live with his wife and children in Shewrapara, Mirpur.
Nahidur’s elder brother, Zahidur Rahman Prince, said they learned from the resort booking bill that Nahidur had reserved a room at Tuptup Resto & Resort from October 16 to 18. He made the booking on October 11 and was scheduled to check out at 1pm on Sunday.
Zahidur said Nahidur told the family that he would travel to Cox’s Bazar on Friday.
After learning about the fire on Saturday, he repeatedly called his younger brother but could not reach him or any other family member.
“We still cannot confirm whether they are alive or dead. We are extremely worried about them,” he said.
Zahidur said Additional Superintendent of Police in Cox’s Bazar, Ahidur Rahman, informed him that a person named Nahid has been reported missing.
The police official also said DNA samples are being collected to identify the bodies, and the remaining four could possibly be Nahidur’s family members, he said.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 8th globally with ‘unhealthy’ air quality
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 8th among the world's most polluted cities on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 177 at 8:50am.
The air quality was classified as "unhealthy", meaning the concentration of pollutants in the air had reached a level that could pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Lahore in Pakistan ranked first with an AQI score of 239, while Delhi in India ranked second with a score of 207, followed by Singapore in Singapore third place with an AQI score of 204.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while 151 to 200 is classified as "unhealthy". A reading between 201 and 300 is considered "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: DSCC launches New Market drive to curb dengue, clear footpaths
item.description:
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has launched a special drive in the New Market area to intensify cleaning activities and clear footpaths as part of efforts to prevent dengue.
DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam led the drive after inaugurating the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme on Saturday. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inspected cleaning and mosquito-control activities in DSCC areas as part of the government’s weekly “Cleaning Day” programme aimed at preventing dengue.
During a surprise inspection on Saturday morning, the prime minister visited Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, the Green Road Government Staff Quarters and the government residential area in Azimpur.
Speaking to students at Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, Tarique Rahman stressed the importance of environmental protection, dengue prevention and maintaining cleanliness. He also encouraged students to plant trees to help reduce environmental pollution.
At the Green Road and Azimpur residential areas, he spoke with residents and urged them to keep their surroundings clean and remove stagnant water to prevent dengue.
He also inspected cleanliness activities along the main roads and surrounding areas and instructed officials to take necessary measures.
Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives State Minister Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Abu Abdullah Md Saleh, DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam and senior government officials accompanied the prime minister during the inspections.
The DSCC said special cleaning drives were conducted simultaneously in all 75 wards as part of the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme. City corporation cleaners and mosquito-control workers, along with local residents, took part in the campaign. Awareness rallies and microphone announcements were also organised throughout the day in different wards to encourage public participation.

item.title: Metro rail's Motijheel to Kamalapur expected to open in July next year
item.description:
The much-anticipated extension of Metro Rail's MRT Line-6 from Motijheel to Kamalapur is expected to open for commercial operations in July next year.
“The overall physical progress of the civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension of MRT Line-6 has reached 84.85%,” Project Director of the Dhaka Mass Transit Development Project (MRT Line-6), Brigadier General (Retd) Md Abdul Wohab, told BSS here on Saturday.
He said mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) works at Kamalapur station are underway, while equipment manufactured abroad will be installed soon after being brought into the country.
According to project details, electro-mechanical works on the extension have progressed by 58%, while construction of the 1.16-kilometre viaduct on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension has been completed, and it has been handed over to Contract Package-7 (CP-07) for rail track installation.
The structural work on Kamalapur MRT Station has also been completed, while MEP and architectural works are underway and are expected to be finished by December 31, 2026.
Meanwhile, work on seven integrated electro-mechanical subsystems under CP-07 is progressing. These include electrical and track systems, signaling, automatic fare collection (AFC), platform screen doors (PSD), telecommunications, lifts and escalators.
The 21.26-kilometre MRT Line-6, extending from Uttara North to Kamalapur, is progressing towards completion. As of September 30, 2026, the physical progress of the Uttara North-Motijheel section stood at 99.67%, while civil construction work on the Motijheel-Kamalapur extension had reached 84.85%.
Once the final section becomes operational, MRT Line-6 will connect Uttara North (Diabari) directly to Kamalapur Railway Station, completing the full 21.26-kilometre route.
The line will have 17 stations, including major stops at Mirpur-10, Agargaon, Farmgate and Dhaka University.
The metro rail began operating on the Uttara–Agargaon section on December 28, 2022. The Agargaon–Motijheel section opened on November 4, 2023. Since the Motijheel section opened, the metro rail has become a vital transport link for Dhaka residents, serving thousands of commuters daily.
Under the current schedule, the first trains depart from Motijheel at 7am and Uttara North at 6:40am.
On average, more than 0.4 million passengers have travelled on the metro rail since its launch, while on September 10, over 0.5 million passengers travelled on the metro, according to project information.
Revenue from ticket sales is also increasing as passenger numbers grow.

item.description:
A parliamentary standing committee on the Planning Ministry has decided to investigate the implementation of the Karnaphuli Tunnel project and the reasons behind its current financial losses.

The committee discussed the tunnel’s feasibility study, implementation process and financial losses, and decided to hold a detailed discussion on the matter at its next meeting.

It expressed hope that the policy, once finalized, would help resolve persistent problems in the appointment process.

item.title: FSCD DG: All 538 fire stations prepared for emergencies during Durga Puja
item.description:
Fire Service and Civil Defense (FSCD) has taken comprehensive measures to ensure fire safety at Durga Puja venues across the country, with all 538 fire stations ready to respond to emergencies during the festival.
Director General of Fire Service and Civil Defense Brigadier General Sultanul Afreen Junaid disclosed the preparations at a press conference held at the department’s headquarters in Dhaka on Saturday.
He said fire stations would remain on standby throughout the festival, monitoring fire safety at puja mandaps in their respective areas and maintaining round-the-clock communication with local administrations and puja committees.
During inspections, fire service personnel will assess fire risks and advise organizers on measures to address them.
They will also publicize the telephone numbers of nearby fire stations and the 102 hotlines for emergency assistance, he added.
Temporary fire stations operating in different locations will remain on high alert, while officials at divisional, district and zonal levels will stay on standby to inspect puja venues and respond to emergencies.
The director general also said the central control room and all divisional control rooms would operate round the clock. Upon receiving an emergency call, they would direct one or more nearby fire stations to respond immediately.
All divisional and district offices, along with fire stations, will coordinate continuously with local administrations and take necessary decisions and implement measures in line with their directions, he said.
At immersion sites, the department will deploy personnel and volunteers, road rescue equipment and ambulances. Lighting units will also be deployed at night where necessary.
Control rooms will be maintained at the department’s headquarters and divisional and district headquarters to ensure continuous communication with fire stations under their respective jurisdictions.
Calling for greater public awareness, Sultanul Afreen said, “Awareness is protection,” and sought the media’s cooperation in raising awareness about fire safety alongside the department’s own efforts.

item.title: Legal notice seeks probe into possible use of dengue as biological weapon
item.description:
A legal notice has been served on the government seeking a high-level scientific investigation into the unusually high dengue mortality in Bangladesh and possible genetic mutations of the virus, including an inquiry into allegations that it could be linked to a covert biological attack.
The notice also demands the establishment of an internationally accredited research laboratory to prevent and investigate biological weapons threats.
Supreme Court lawyer Md Mahmudul Hasan Mamun served the notice on Saturday in the public interest.
It was addressed to the secretaries of the ministries of defence, home affairs, health and family welfare, and foreign affairs, as well as the administrators of Dhaka North and South city corporations. A copy was also sent to the United Nations resident coordinator in Bangladesh.
The notice describes dengue as a severe public health crisis rather than a routine illness, arguing that the recurring deaths and growing number of cases warrant investigation beyond conventional mosquito-control measures.
Citing books on biological warfare and medical research, Mamun, who is also studying for a Master of Public Health degree, refers to historical accounts of plans to use disease-carrying insects in biological attacks.
The notice cites The A to Z of Nuclear, Biological, and Chemical Warfare (2019), by Benjamin C Garrett and John Hart, which discusses a Japanese military plan during World War II, codenamed “Operation PX”. According to the notice, the plan involved releasing insects carrying pathogens linked to dengue, plague, cholera and typhus along the US coast.
It also refers to Anthony Tu’s book Chemical and Biological Weapons and Terrorism (2018), which the notice says discusses the classification of dengue virus among biological agents considered for weaponisation by the US military.
Another reference is Advances in Biological and Chemical Terrorism Countermeasures (2008), edited by Ronald J Kendall and other experts. The notice cites the publication in support of its concerns about the potential misuse of disease-causing agents.
The notice argues that Bangladesh’s high population density and mosquito prevalence, alongside the reported severity of recent dengue outbreaks, warrant an urgent scientific and forensic investigation. It calls for epidemiologists, virologists and public health specialists to examine the virus’s genetic characteristics, origin and transmission mechanisms to determine whether there is evidence of deliberate or artificial modification.
However, the notice does not present evidence establishing that the dengue outbreak in Bangladesh resulted from a biological attack.
Mamun also cites Bangladesh’s obligations under international law, noting that the country is a signatory to the Biological Weapons Convention (BWC). He refers to Articles I and X of the convention, which prohibit biological weapons and address the peaceful use of biological science, as well as United Nations Security Council Resolution 1540 of 2004, which requires states to take measures against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.
The notice further invokes Articles 18(1) and 32 of the Constitution of Bangladesh, concerning the state’s responsibility to improve public health and the right to life.
It asks the authorities to arrange an expert-led genetic and forensic investigation into the dengue virus within 10 days to assess whether there is any evidence of an artificial biological attack. It also calls for the immediate establishment of a high-security laboratory for research into biological weapons prevention and comprehensive, science-based measures to control Aedes mosquitoes.
The notice warns that failure to meet the demands could lead to a public interest litigation petition before the High Court Division of the Supreme Court under Article 102 of the Constitution, seeking measures to protect public health, national security and citizens’ lives.

item.title: Russia hails Trump waiving sanctions as ‘historic’
item.description:
Russia on Saturday hailed US President Donald Trump’s move to waive new sanctions on it as “historic,” as Ukraine worries he is taking Moscow’s side in Europe’s worst conflict since World War II.
Trump signed an executive order Friday that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia’s energy revenues amid a clash with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
The decision came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine -- especially its capital, Kyiv -- in the fifth year of its offensive, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
“The Trump administration’s suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment,” Kirill Dmitriev, envoy for Russian President Vladimir Putin, said on social media.
The Lindsey Graham Act -- named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill -- targeted Russia’s energy and defense sectors, as well as Putin and the so-called “shadow fleet” of tankers used by Moscow to circumvent Western sanctions.
The Kremlin and Putin have not yet reacted to the move, which is a major diplomatic win for Moscow.
Dmitriev said the act would have caused “serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets.”
Trump’s waiver comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease existing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.
He announced the executive order Friday, shortly after Putin appeared in military uniform and said Moscow aims to capture the rest of east Ukraine.
US-led talks to end the war in Ukraine have not led to a breakthrough. Both Putin and Zelensky have frustrated Trump in the past with a lack of progress in halting the grinding war.
The move is bound to spook Ukraine’s European allies, who worry the White House is taking the Kremlin’s side.
Zelensky rallied his allies Friday on a visit to Brussels for a European Union summit, urging them to keep financing Ukraine’s fight and insisting he was standing up for his country amid the row with Trump.
Russian forces struck Ukraine’s southern city of Kherson Saturday after Trump’s announcement, killing one person and wounding 22, local officials said.
Russia has increased strikes on Kyiv in recent weeks, squeezing the city as Ukrainians brace for another winter of war.
Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defenses ahead of winter.
Russia controls large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine and Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine by force.
“On the whole I see a positive trend in the operations of the troop groupings,” Putin told army leaders Friday, dressed in military attire.
“Undoubtedly, one of the main objectives remains the liberation of the Donetsk People’s Republic,” he added, using the Kremlin’s name for the eastern Donetsk region.
European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky Friday as he grappled with Trump.
“This is no time to withdraw support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia’s sanctions,” said European Council chief Antonio Costa.
“Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure.”
European concerns have been heightened by disruptions to a critical US-provided satellite system that has hampered Ukraine’s ability to counter Russia’s intense bombardments.

item.title: Former additional secretary found dead at Officers Club
item.description:
The body of former additional secretary Md Mosharraf Hossain was recovered from a building under construction at the Officers Club in Dhaka’s Ramna area on Friday morning.
Police recovered the body around 11:45am.

According to reports, he arrived at the club around 10am with his youngest daughter. He left her near the swimming pool, beside the building under construction, and entered the structure.

Sheikh Zahidul Islam, deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Ramna division, said Mosharraf had poor eyesight and apparently fell from the third floor into an open space on the ground floor.

item.title: National Parliament committee proposes annual assessments to enhance education quality
item.description:
The Standing Committee on the Ministry of Education of the 13th National Parliament has recommended introducing an annual assessment system aligned with international standards to improve quality of education and move beyond artificial competition over pass rates.
At its first meeting held at the National Parliament Building on September 10, the committee proposed a series of measures to ensure transparency in education spending, tackle irregularities and corruption, investigate declining secondary-level enrolment, strengthen teacher training and expand technical education.
Chairman of the committee and Member of Parliament Md Salim Bhuiyan told Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS) at the Secretariat yesterday that the previous government had focused on numerical indicators and pass rates rather than genuine educational quality.
“Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government does not believe in this artificial competition. We want to ensure genuine quality in education in the country,” he said.
He stressed the need for annual assessments, a modern curriculum and evaluations of learning outcomes at three- or six-month intervals to bring students in line with international standards.
Further recommendations and details of the government's education roadmap will be presented at a press conference, he added.
Committee member Reza Kibria also emphasized setting specific annual benchmarks to ensure Bangladeshi students perform competitively in international assessments, particularly in mathematics and science.
Members proposed a long-term national education vision, modelled on Malaysia, to prevent frequent changes to education policies, curricula and textbooks following changes in government.
According to the meeting minutes, the government has proposed a budget of Tk57,301.68 crore for the Secondary and Higher Education Division in the 2026-27 fiscal year, 42.7% higher than the previous revised budget.
The initiatives discussed included distributing laptops to approximately 40,000 students who achieved a Golden GPA in 2026 and bringing seven million female students under a Tk4,000 crore scholarship program to promote girls’ education and reduce dropout rates.
The committee also acknowledged the transfer of outstanding dues to the bank accounts of around 70,000 retired teachers and employees through the Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) and iBAS systems.
In the initial phase, each teacher is receiving an average of Tk5 lakh.
The committee thanked Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for providing Tk2,000 crore in special assistance to address the crisis involving teachers' welfare and retirement benefits.
It recommended expediting MPO enlistment for eligible non-MPO institutions and long-serving teachers, reducing bureaucratic delays and investigating the significant decline in secondary-level enrolment.
Technical and Madrasah Education Division Secretary (routine charge) Shamsur Rahman Khan informed the meeting that technical education enrolment reached 19.16% in 2025, with a target of 30% by 2030.
Other decisions included field visits by committee members to inspect educational institutions, mandatory attendance of education board heads and National University representatives at future meetings, and faster settlement of outstanding allowances, subject to budget availability.
Educationists have welcomed the proposals, particularly the shift towards measurable learning outcomes and international standards, as potentially significant steps towards improving education quality.

item.title: Speakers: Climate-vulnerable countries must not be pushed into debt trap
item.description:
Climate-vulnerable countries must not be pushed into a new debt trap in the name of climate adaptation, speakers said at a human chain program in Mongla on Friday.
They said developed countries and corporations continue to profit from fossil fuel-dependent economies, while farmers, workers and climate-vulnerable nations bear the brunt of cyclones, droughts, river erosion and crop losses.
The speakers called for a just transition to green energy, environmental protection, climate justice and public ownership of resources.
The human chain program was held at Mithekhali Bazar in Mongla, coinciding with the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, scheduled for October 12-18. The event focused on the question of whose interests the global economy serves.
Dharitri Rakkhay Amra, Pashur River Waterkeeper, Udayan Youth Sangha, and Waterkeepers Bangladesh jointly organised the program.
Nur Alam Sheikh, a central leader of DHORA and Pashur River Waterkeeper, presided over the event. Speakers included Prof Nazrul Islam, labour leader Nazmul Haque, DHORA leader Molla Al Mamun, farmer leader Asaduzzaman Tito, SM Jane Alam Babu of Udayan Youth Sangha, youth leaders Sheikh Sifatullah Shuvo and Arafat Durjoy, and Mehedi Hasan of Waterkeepers Bangladesh.
Nazmul Haque said developing countries were struggling to repay foreign loans and interest while meeting essential spending needs in education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection. High interest rates, rising energy prices and climate-related disasters were further aggravating the crisis, he said.
“If people’s fundamental rights are curtailed to repay loans, who is development for?” he asked, stressing that public needs must take precedence over lenders’ conditions.
In his address, Nur Alam Sheikh said communities affected by climate change should receive fair compensation, not loans, for the losses and damage they suffer. “We must build a world for people, not for profit,” he said, calling for adequate climate financing and investment in renewable energy.
He also urged the government to ensure that food was treated as a fundamental human right rather than a source of corporate profit, promote environmentally friendly agriculture and ensure a just transition to green energy.
“Financing renewable energy is financing climate action,” he said, calling for an immediate shift to renewable energy.

item.title: Durga Puja begins in Gopalganj, Sunamganj with festive fervour
item.description:
The five-day Sharadiya Durga Puja, the biggest religious festival of the Hindu community, began in Gopalganj on Friday with Maha Shashthi rituals, including the invocation and ceremonial welcome of the goddess.
According to the traditional calendar, this year's celebrations will continue for six days, ending on Wednesday, with Bijoya Dashami and the immersion of idols.
The festivities began gathering momentum on Thursday evening, when temples and puja mandaps across the district were illuminated with colourful lights and decorated with elaborate pandals, ornate gates and eye-catching designs. The sound of drums and conch shells added to the festive atmosphere as devotees visited the mandaps to offer prayers, take photographs and celebrate.
Priests performed Shashthi rituals on Friday morning, formally welcoming Goddess Durga to the mortal world from her heavenly abode on Mount Kailash, accompanied by her four children — Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik and Ganesha.
The goddess's face will be unveiled at the mandaps on Saturday, marking Maha Saptami. Saptami rituals will continue tomorrow, followed by Ashtami on Monday, Navami on Tuesday and Dashami on Wednesday.
This year, Durga Puja is being celebrated at 1,288 mandaps across Gopalganj's five upazilas and four municipalities. Security has been strengthened at the venues to ensure peaceful celebrations.
Sanjay Sikdar, general secretary of the Gopalganj district unit of the Puja Udjapan Parishad, said devotees would bid farewell to the goddess through idol immersion on Dashami, before welcoming her again the following year.
Dipankar Chakraborty, a priest at Shahapara Temple in the town, said the goddess arrived this year riding a horse and would depart by boat. According to traditional beliefs, the two modes of transport symbolise social uncertainty and agricultural prosperity, respectively.
Durga Puja is also being celebrated at 445 mandaps across Sunamganj. The five-day festival began on Friday with Maha Shashthi and will conclude on Bijoya Dashami.
The Special Response Battalion (SRB) has stepped up surveillance on social media to prevent rumours and misinformation that could disrupt communal harmony during Durga Puja.
Its cyber team is monitoring Facebook, Instagram and other platforms around the clock, said Wing Commander Tajminur Rahman Chowdhury, commander of SRB-9 Sylhet.
He made the remarks on Friday after inspecting security arrangements at the Durgabari Puja Mandap in Sunamganj town.
He said bomb disposal teams were ready to respond to reports of suspected explosives near puja mandaps. Drone surveillance, special patrols and dog squads have been deployed, while speedboats remain on standby for remote areas. Helicopter support will be provided if necessary.
A strong security cordon has been established across the four districts under SRB-9 to maintain law and order, he added. The force will remain on duty until Bijoya Dashami, the final day of the festival.

Eighteen passenger railway coaches arrive from India
item.description:
Eighteen broad-gauge passenger railway coaches imported from India entered Bangladesh through the Darshana-Jaynagar border in Chuadanga at 3pm on Friday.
After completing customs formalities at Darshana, the coaches will be taken to Bangladesh Railway’s workshop in Saidpur for inspection before being added to the railway fleet.
The coaches began their journey from Kapurthala in India’s Punjab state on Monday, October 12. They remained at Ranaghat Station in Kolkata before departing on Friday afternoon.
After completing formalities at India’s Gede border checkpoint, the coaches entered Bangladesh through the Darshana-Jaynagar border. Officials of Bangladesh Railway’s Pakshey division subsequently took charge of the shipment.
The coaches have been painted red and green. The shipment includes 3 air-conditioned chair coaches, air-conditioned berth coaches, 4 luggage vans and 11 Shovon chair coaches.
In May 2024, the Bangladesh government signed an agreement with India’s RITES Limited under a project to purchase broad-gauge railway coaches.
The coaches were procured from RITES Limited in India. A total of 200 coaches will be collected from India in several phases and added to Bangladesh Railway’s fleet.
Robiul Islam, divisional mechanical engineer of Bangladesh Railway’s Pakshey division, said 18 broad-gauge passenger coaches had entered Bangladesh from India on Friday.
He said the coaches belonged to different categories and that the government had taken the initiative to improve the quality of passenger services.

item.title: Two arrested over mob killing in Satkhira, prime accused at large
item.description:
A murder case has been filed over the lyincing of Wahiduzzaman Shamim, a man with mental health issues, in Debhata, Satkhira, following allegations of religious insult and incitement through Facebook Live and posts.
Shamim’s elder brother, Abdul Jalil, filed the case with Debhata police station on Thursday night, naming 10 people, with Fazlul Haque Ameni of Parulia named as the prime accused. Another 200-250 unidentified people have also been accused.
Police have arrested two people in connection with the case, including Moktar Hossain and Asadul Molla.
According to the case statement and family members, Shamim became involved in a domestic dispute with his wife on Monday evening and allegedly used abusive language. A local person later circulated an audio recording of the exchange on social media.
Claiming that the recording contained derogatory remarks, local resident Fazlul Haque Ameni went live on Facebook and called on the people to attack Shamim.
A mob subsequently attacked the family’s home and vandalised property.
Shamim was also assaulted near Subarnabad market, according to his elder brother, Abdul Jalil.
Following the attack, Shamim returned home and consumed poison, his family said.
He was taken to the chamber of a local physician, MA Sabur, in the Kuliya area, where he received treatment and was kept under observation.
On Tuesday, a mob entered the doctor’s chamber and attacked him again. Police intervened, rescued Shamim and took him to Sakhipur Health Complex.
However, the violence did not end there.
According to the family, another large mob entered the health facility, assaulted Shamim and dragged him outside.
Jalil alleged that Ameni led the crowd, which he estimated numbered more than 1,000 people.
The attackers allegedly slammed Shamim against a wall and beat him severely.
Police subsequently recovered him and transferred him to Satkhira Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
OC Shahin confirmed that Shamim had been attacked again after police initially rescued him.
“At 8:30pm, an agitated mob, or ‘Tawhidi Janata’, whatever one might call them, arrived and assaulted him again,” he said.
Shamim’s family described the killing as deliberate and demanded action against those responsible for mobilising the crowd.
“They incited people against him using a provocative video/audio clip, and then deliberately and systematically beat him to death,” Sagar said.
Sagar said his brother had completed his Honours and Master’s degrees in History at Jagannath University.
According to the family, Shamim developed mental health problems after being drugged by criminals during a bus journey several years ago.
He had experienced periods of mental instability for around a decade and had been receiving medical treatment.
The family said his condition had affected his personal life, including his first marriage.
Shamim leaves behind two sons, one from each marriage.
Sagar questioned why his brother had been subjected to mob violence instead of being dealt with through the legal system.
“If the law had punished him, we would have accepted it. But why should my brother be beaten to death without any trial?” he said.
The victim’s family also alleged that local Jamaat-e-Islami activists were involved in mobilising people during the initial attack.
Sagar claimed that some participants had gathered at a local Jamaat office before proceeding to the family’s home.
He alleged that local party leaders and activists were among those involved.
However, Kamrul Islam Gazi, president of the Ward 8 Jamaat-e-Islami unit in Parulia Union, denied the allegations.
He told BBC Bangla that local residents, rather than Jamaat activists, had assaulted Shamim.
“No... it was the local residents,” he said when asked whether party members were involved.
Gazi said he had heard that Shamim was beaten after being taken for treatment following his consumption of poison.
The family’s allegations against Jamaat members have not been independently established.
As of 3pm on Thursday, no murder case had been filed, according to police.
OC Shahin said police had contacted the victim’s family and were expecting them to visit the police station to lodge a complaint.
Sagar also said the family intended to file a case later in the day.
Police said the investigation was continuing and that legal action would be taken against those identified as responsible.

item.title: Two women killed in road accident in Shyamoli
item.description:
Two women were killed after being hit by a speeding vehicle while crossing the road in the capital’s Shyamoli area early Friday.
One of the victims was identified as Mukta, 40, while the identity of the other woman, estimated to be around 45, has yet to be confirmed.
Both were reportedly residents of the area.
The accident occurred beneath the overbridge near Shyamoli intersection early on Friday.
Police said a speeding vehicle struck the two women as they were crossing the road and fled the scene. One woman died on the spot.
Mohammadpur police rushed to the scene and rescued Mukta in an injured condition before taking her to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where she died while undergoing treatment.
The bodies have been kept in the hospital morgue for autopsies.
Mohammadpur police station Officer-in-Charge Abdul Halim said police had identified one of the victims but were still trying to establish the other woman’s identity.
He added that police were also working to identify the vehicle involved in the accident.

Faridpur Zila Parishad installs 60kW rooftop solar systems
item.description:
Faridpur Zila Parishad has installed rooftop solar power systems with a combined capacity of 60 kilowatts (kW) at two government facilities, with surplus electricity being supplied to the national grid through a net metering system.
The initiative aims to expand renewable energy use in public buildings, reduce electricity costs and promote environmentally sustainable energy solutions.
The systems were inaugurated and a bilateral agreement was signed at 1pm on Thursday, following directives from the Local Government Division.
Under the project, a 40kW solar power system has been installed on the roof of the parishad's engineering department building, while a 20kW system has been set up at the Sadar VIP Dak Bungalow.
Marsh Power Technology Ltd, a company listed with the power distribution authorities, implemented the project. Under the agreement, the company will be responsible for maintaining and repairing the systems for the next 20 years.
A bilateral agreement was also signed between Faridpur Zila Parishad and the Faridpur Sales and Distribution Division of West Zone Power Distribution Company Ltd (WZPDCL-1) to facilitate the supply of solar-generated electricity to the national grid through net metering.
Faridpur Deputy Commissioner Mazharul Islam attended the inauguration as the chief guest. Among others, Zila Parishad Administrator Md Afzal Hossain Khan Palash, Chief Executive Officer Md Bakahid Hossain, Superintendent of Police Shahriar Mohammad Miyazi, Faridpur Sadar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Meshkatul Jannat Rabeya, Executive Officer Sanjida Sultana, Local Government Engineering Department Executive Engineer Mohammad Azharul Islam and WZPDCL-1 Executive Engineer Pranab Chandra Debnath were present.
Speaking at the event, Mazharul Islam stressed the need to expand the use of clean energy to address the adverse effects of climate change and ensure a safe environment for future generations.
“Expanding solar power use across both the public and private sectors can help build an energy-efficient and environmentally friendly Bangladesh,” he said.

item.title: Record 964 Durga Puja pandals in Rangpur, elaborate displays draw crowds in Khulna
item.description:
Durga Puja will be celebrated at a record 964 pandals across Rangpur district and 818 venues in Khulna district this year, with elaborate idol displays drawing crowds and authorities stepping up security to ensure peaceful festivities.
In Rangpur, artisans are putting the finishing touches to idols as organisers decorate pandals ahead of the celebrations. The district will host celebrations at 964 pandals across the city and eight upazilas, the highest number recorded so far.
Of the total, 164 pandals are in Rangpur city’s 33 wards, 10 more than last year, while the remaining 800 are spread across the eight upazilas.
Taraganj has the highest number of pandals among the upazilas, with 165, followed by Mithapukur with 151, Badarganj with 125, Pirganj with 100, Gangachara with 99, Rangpur Sadar with 94, Pirgachha with 91 and Kaunia with 75.
The celebrations will feature devotional music, clothing and prasad distribution, arati competitions and processions marking Bijoya Dashami, said Advocate Prashanta Kumar Roy, general secretary of the Rangpur metropolitan committee of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad.
Rangpur Superintendent of Police Mohammad Mozammel Haque said extensive security measures had been taken, with law enforcement personnel to be deployed before the festival begins. Police have held meetings with puja committees to coordinate security arrangements, while volunteers will assist law enforcement agencies at the pandals.
In Khulna, two temples in Dumuria Upazila have drawn particular attention for their elaborate displays featuring 201 and 152 idols.
The century-old Kharsang Kalibot Tala Sarbojonin Puja Temple in Kharsang village of Rudaghara Union has arranged 201 idols, while the Kharsang Mikshimil Sahapara Sarbojonin Puja Temple, near Mikshimil Bazar less than half a kilometre away, has created 152 idols.
The displays depict episodes from Hindu mythology and religious epics, including scenes from the Ramayana, stories of Lord Krishna, the nine forms of Goddess Durga and other religious figures.
Work on the idols began four months ago. Shimul Das, a sculptor from Satkhira, made 152 idols at the Sahapara temple for Tk3.5 lakh, while Abhilash Mondal created 201 idols at Kharsang for the same amount. Painting work is still underway, but visitors have already begun arriving in large numbers.
School students Tripti Roy, Chaiti Roy and Tapati Chowdhury said they had visited both temples before school to see the displays.
Subrata Sarkar, general secretary of the Kharsang temple, said the two venues had the largest idol displays in the area and were expected to attract substantial crowds. He added that the century-old temple had not received government assistance for its development.
Professor Kartik Chandra Saha, president of the Sahapara temple committee, said the annual celebration had continued peacefully for 52 years with donations from local devotees.
Durga Puja will be celebrated at 225 venues across Dumuria’s 14 unions, said Tutul Kundu, president of the Dumuria Upazila Puja Udjapan Front.
Khulna Superintendent of Police Sardar Omar Faruk said security arrangements had been made at all 818 venues across the district, including 89 designated as particularly important. Uniformed police will be deployed at every venue, alongside members of the Coast Guard, the SRB and plainclothes law enforcement teams. Banners displaying emergency contact numbers will also be placed at the venues.
Authorities in both districts have urged puja committees, law enforcement agencies and people from all communities to work together to ensure peaceful celebrations.

item.title: Bangladesh ranks 84th in Global Hunger Index 2026
item.description:
Bangladesh ranked 84th in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2026, scoring 19.2 and remaining in the “moderate” hunger category, as child undernutrition continues to pose a significant public health challenge despite progress in reducing stunting over the past 2 decades.
The index shows that 8.2% of Bangladesh’s population is undernourished, while 24% of children under 5 suffer from stunting, or low height for their age.
Another 12.9% of children under 5 experience wasting, or low weight for their height, and 3% of children die before reaching the age of 5.
Bangladesh performed better than India and Pakistan but lagged behind Nepal in the regional comparison.
India ranked 100th with a score of 24.1, while Pakistan placed 106th with 25.5, putting both countries in the “serious” hunger category. Nepal ranked 72nd with a score of 14.5, remaining in the “moderate” category.
A lower GHI score indicates lower levels of hunger and undernutrition, although rankings also depend on the performance of other countries included in the assessment.
One of Bangladesh’s most notable achievements is the reduction in child stunting over the past 2 decades.
The proportion of children under 5 affected by stunting fell from 54.9% in 2000 to 24% in the latest assessment, a decline of 30.9 percentage points.
However, the continued prevalence of wasting among nearly 13% of children under 5 highlights the need to address both chronic and acute malnutrition.
Stunting reflects long-term nutritional deprivation and can affect physical growth, cognitive development and educational outcomes. Wasting, meanwhile, is associated with inadequate nutrition and illness and can increase the risk of death among young children.
Public health experts say improvements in food availability alone are not enough to eliminate malnutrition. Dietary diversity, maternal nutrition, access to safe water and sanitation, health care services and household purchasing power also play crucial roles.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Dr Mehbuba Nur Protha, district technical coordinator at FIVDB, said: “Although Bangladesh has made significant progress in reducing child stunting, the high prevalence of child wasting remains a serious concern, which underscores the need to strengthen maternal and child health and nutrition services at primary health care centers, ensure access to affordable, diverse diets, and improve access to safe water, sanitation, and health care, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized communities.”
The findings come amid wider concerns over the impact of economic pressures, climate-related disasters and disruptions to food systems on household food security.
For low-income families, rising food prices can make it difficult to maintain a balanced diet, even when staple foods remain available. Households may prioritize rice and other inexpensive staples over protein-rich foods, fruits, vegetables and other nutrient-dense items.
Nutrition specialists say children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers are particularly vulnerable when households cannot afford diverse and nutritious diets.
Dr Khondaker Golam Moazzem, research director of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), said: “Rising food prices and stagnant household purchasing power can force low-income families to compromise on dietary diversity, making nutritious food increasingly unaffordable and worsening the risk of child malnutrition.”
Climate change is another concern, particularly for communities exposed to floods, cyclones, river erosion and salinity intrusion. Such hazards can damage crops, disrupt food supply chains, reduce household incomes and undermine access to safe drinking water.
Experts working on climate resilience and food security could help assess how these risks affect nutrition among children and vulnerable communities.
The 2026 report warns that global hunger is rising again, with conflict, climate shocks and economic crises threatening food security.
The GHI uses 4 indicators to assess hunger: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and under-5 mortality. Together, they capture both the availability of adequate food and the nutritional and health outcomes associated with hunger.
The index is published annually by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe, with research support from the Institute for International Law of Peace and Armed Conflict (IFHV).
Under the index’s classification system, scores below 10 indicate low hunger; scores from 10 to 19.9 indicate moderate hunger; scores from 20 to 34.9 indicate serious hunger; scores from 35 to 49.9 indicate alarming hunger; and scores of 50 or above indicate extremely alarming hunger.
Bangladesh’s score of 19.2 places it near the upper end of the moderate category, underscoring the need for sustained action to improve nutrition outcomes.
Nutrition experts say Bangladesh needs stronger coordination between food security, public health, social protection, agriculture and climate adaptation programs to make further progress.
Measures could include expanding nutrition services for mothers and young children, improving access to affordable protein-rich foods, strengthening school and community nutrition programs, and supporting climate-resilient agriculture.
Better targeting of social safety-net programs and improved monitoring of child growth could also help identify vulnerable households and direct assistance where it is most needed.
While the reduction in stunting represents substantial progress, the latest figures indicate that Bangladesh still faces significant challenges in ensuring that all children receive adequate and nutritious food.
The country’s performance in future assessments will depend not only on food availability but also on whether vulnerable households can afford diverse diets and access the health care, sanitation and social support necessary for healthy growth.

item.title: Puja Udjapan Parishad reports 34 attacks ahead of Durga Puja
item.description:
At least 34 incidents of idol vandalism, temple attacks and other related violence have been reported at Durga Puja venues across Bangladesh ahead of the Hindu community’s biggest religious festival, the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad and the Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee have said.
The two organisations called for effective measures to prevent further attacks and ensure the security of religious and ethnic minorities throughout the year.
The allegations were raised at a press conference organised by the two bodies at the Dhakeshwari National Temple complex in Dhaka on Thursday morning ahead of Sharadiya Durga Puja.
The leaders expressed hope that the festival would be celebrated peacefully and without disruption, stressing that religious festivals should unite people from all communities and reflect Bangladesh’s longstanding tradition of communal harmony.
They said they envisioned a society where Eid, Durga Puja, Christmas, Buddha Purnima and other religious and social festivals could be celebrated in a secular environment without fear or the need for police protection.
A written statement was presented at the meeting by Shubhashish Kumar Biswas (Sadhan), general secretary of the Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee.
Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad General Secretary Santosh Sharma said most cases filed over attacks in the previous year had resulted in punishment, with legal proceedings initiated and charge sheets submitted.
“This year, the notable development is that a total of 34 incidents involving idol vandalism, attacks on temples and other related incidents have been reported so far,” he said.
Sharma acknowledged that negligence by some Puja committees had contributed to a few incidents. Citing an incident in Netrokona, he said security arrangements had been maintained throughout the night, but no one was on guard at dawn when the incident occurred at around 5:00am.
He also said the temple's CCTV camera was defective and therefore failed to provide surveillance.
Despite these shortcomings, the local administration had taken appropriate measures, he said, adding that arrests had been made in 11 of the 34 incidents and action had been taken in the others. Some incidents were relatively minor, he added. “We are satisfied so far,” Sharma said.
However, he stressed the need for justice for major attacks against the Hindu community over Bangladesh’s 55-year history, citing the Ramu violence, the Nasirnagar attacks, the 2021 Comilla incident and the attacks in Sunamganj.
“Even today, we are demanding justice for all these incidents and exemplary punishment for those responsible,” he said.
Among those present were Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad President Basudeb Dhar, General Secretary Santosh Sharma, former presidents Advocate Subrata Chowdhury and Kajal Debnath, former general secretary Dr Chandranath Poddar, adviser Bires Chandra Saha, and Mahanagar Sarbojanin Puja Committee President Gopal Chandra Debnath, along with other leaders.
According to the written statement, incidents of idol vandalism and attacks on temples have been reported in several districts, including Sylhet, Rajbari, Panchagarh, Netrokona and Tangail, during preparations for the festival.
The statement also cited a theft at a historic Kali temple in Faridpur and attacks and looting targeting homes, shops and temples belonging to members of the Hindu community in Sunamganj.
It further reported a robbery in Naogaon involving individuals posing as intelligence agency personnel.
The organisations acknowledged that law enforcement agencies had acted promptly in several cases and arrested a number of suspects. However, they stressed that lasting protection for minorities could not depend solely on police intervention.
They called for a broader commitment to secular values and stronger social resistance to communal violence.
“Security for five days of Puja is not enough; security must be ensured for 365 days a year,” the leaders said, emphasising that building a discrimination-free Bangladesh required promoting secular values and ensuring justice for perpetrators of violence.
The written statement said the administration had assured organisers of full cooperation in holding Durga Puja celebrations nationwide. Authorities had promised adequate security, while relevant public service agencies had pledged support and assured organisers that any problems would be addressed promptly.
The Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad has also issued 22-point guidelines to its district- and upazila-level units to ensure the smooth organisation of the festival.
At the meeting, the organisations reiterated their eight-point demands to protect the rights and existence of religious and ethnic minorities in Bangladesh.
The demands include enacting a minority protection law, establishing a national minority commission and forming a dedicated ministry for minority affairs. They also called for proper implementation of the Vested Property Return Act.
The organisations urged the authorities to remove bureaucratic obstacles to the return of vested properties and restore ownership and possession of land to affected individuals within the stipulated timeframe, in accordance with tribunal verdicts.
They also demanded representation of minorities in the government, parliament and all representative bodies in proportion to their share of the population.
Other demands include enacting a law to protect debottor properties, or assets dedicated to religious institutions; passing an anti-discrimination law; and transforming the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust into a foundation.
The organisations further urged the government to issue a gazette notification declaring the three days from Ashtami to Dashami during Durga Puja as public holidays.
According to the written statement, draft bills on protecting debottor properties and eliminating discrimination had already been finalised.

item.title: Expatriates take alternative routes to Riyadh despite extra costs, risks
item.description:
Mamun, a resident of Noakhali Sadar, works as a truck driver for a company in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. After living abroad for five years, he returned to Bangladesh for the first time two months ago.
His return flight to Riyadh was scheduled for October 11, but it was cancelled. He booked another ticket for October 12, only for that flight to be cancelled as well.
With just five days left on his visa, Mamun grew increasingly worried. He finally secured a ticket for a flight to Medina on October 15.
Despite fears over the ongoing conflict, he is relieved to be able to return to Saudi Arabia.
Speaking at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport’s (HSIA) departure terminal, Mamun said: “My visa is about to expire, but I could not leave. I was extremely worried. Finally, I can travel via Medina.”
However, the alternative route means more time, expense and hassle. From Medina, he will have to travel by bus for 12 to 14 hours to reach Riyadh.
“We have already faced so much trouble, and now there is more waiting for us in Medina. Travelling from there to Riyadh will take 12 to 14 hours by bus, with additional expenses. But we have no choice. We have to go, so we are accepting the extra costs and risks. Please pray for us,” he said.
Parvez, an expatriate worker from Manikganj, has faced similar difficulties following repeated flight cancellations.
“We have been through a lot of hassle. One flight after another was cancelled, and I thought I would not be able to travel at all. Now I have to go via Medina,” he said.
With around seven days remaining on his visa, Parvez decided to travel rather than risk further delays.
“I know there are security concerns, but we have no choice. We have to go,” he said.
Al Amin, from Nabinagar in Brahmanbaria, said flights to Riyadh and Dammam had been cancelled, leaving passengers uncertain about when services would resume.
“All flights to Riyadh and Dammam have been cancelled, and nobody knows when they will resume. Our visas are also about to expire. What are we supposed to do? We are being forced to travel via Medina and then take a bus to Riyadh, which will take around 14 hours,” he said.
“If we could fly directly, we would not have to go through all this trouble. But what can we do? We have no other option if we want to keep our jobs,” he added.
A visit to the airport found expatriate workers travelling to Riyadh via Medina, with many whose visas were nearing expiry changing their tickets to take the alternative route.
The Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight to Medina was scheduled to depart at 3:55pm, and passengers began arriving at the airport by noon. As they prepared to board, their earlier anxiety gave way to relief at finally being able to travel.
Passengers said they had to make repeated trips from their villages to change their tickets. The alternative route and additional travel expenses were costing them an extra Tk20,000-25,000.
Despite the added costs and security concerns, many were relieved to be able to leave Bangladesh before their visas expired.
On October 10, Riyadh airport came under attack by Yemen’s Houthi rebels. Dammam airport was subsequently targeted by a missile, disrupting flight operations.
By Thursday, over 100 flights had been cancelled from HSIA, leaving more than 15,000 expatriate Bangladeshis stranded.

item.title: Feed Industry in trouble as prices of raw materials increase
item.description:
Prices of different raw materials used in poultry feed recently increased by 9% to 40%. In response, feed manufacturers have raised the prices of their products by a meagre 7%. Many are not recovering the cost of production. Rising global prices of raw materials have resulted in margins being squeezed.
However, some critics have been quick to allege that the increase in feed price has no rationale other than profit maximisation. They claim that the price increase has harmed farmers, and increased the prices of chicken and eggs.
Poultry feed manufacturers argue that the price increases are not enough to conver their increased costs. As the industry is very competitive, each feed company is afraid that increasing its price will lead to a loss of market share. Because competition is intense, the feed industry operates with a very thin profit margin.
According to the late September 2026 data, the price of maize increased from Tk31.3 to Tk38.8 (per kg), soya bean meal from Tk58 to Tk66 (per kg). Maize and soya bean meal are the major ingredients of poultry feed. Though the price of maize increased by 24% and the price of soya bean meal increased by 14%, the price of poultry feed was raised only 7%, from Tk68 per kg to Tk72.50 per kg.
Other feed materials have also become more expensive. De-oiled rice bran from Tk26 to Tk33 (per kg), rice bran from Tk33 to Tk39 (per kg), and mustard oil cake from Tk36.50 to Tk39.70 (per kg).
The increasing cost of poultry feed inevitably increases the prices of chicken and eggs. Poultry industry stakeholders suggest reducing taxes on the industry to arrest the upward price spiral.
Mosharaf Hossain Chowdhury, president of Bangladesh Poultry Industries Association (BPIA) and managing director of Asta Feed Mill, mentioned that the price of soya bean meal rose 20% or $100 to $530 (per ton) in the international market in August. “The price of feed was increased by Tk2 per kg in late August and Tk2.50 per kg in September. Yet, feed mill owners are making losses,” he argued.
The first increase in raw material prices came when the maize price increased in Brazil and the shipping cost also went up. Moshiur Rahman, managing director of Paragon Agro Industries, said: “Raw material price increase elsewhere or supply disruption immediately affects the Bangladesh market.”
Ihtesham B Shahjahan, managing director of Quality Feeds Limited explained that it requires almost 80 ingredients to prepare poultry feeds and their prices increased by up to 40%.
BPIA leaders told this author that in the budget for fiscal year 2025-26, the rate of corporate income tax for the poultry sector increased from 15% to 27.5%. As a result, the net profit has already become very low, and feed mills must pass cost increases on to farmers.
ATM Habibur Rahman, chief commercial officer of Akij Feed Mill, said that the price of maize recently increased from $235 to $290 per ton. “If prices of all ingredients increase, how can we sell the poultry feed at same price?” he questioned.
Md Anwarul Haque, general secretary of Feed Industries Association of Bangladesh and managing director of Padma Feed Mill, pointed out that the poultry feed industry is imports 65% of its raw materials. “The prices of feeds have been raised only slightly, in comparison to the increases in prices of raw materials. We are in a survival mode now,” he added.
A recent Bangladesh Bank report reviewed the cost structure of a few companies, and calculated the cost of production of broiler grower feed at Tk61.77 per kg, and sales price at Tk69.75 per kg.
Around 150 companies produce 7.5 million tons of animal feeds, 70% of which is consumed by the poultry sector. A large number of informal feed mills also produce an additional volume of feed.
A study by Bangladesh Agriculture University predicted that the demand for animal feed will increase to 10 million tons by 2030 and that the poultry sector will account for 65% of it.

item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) is setting up 18 base camps and strengthening patrols to ensure security at around 1,800 puja mandaps located within eight kilometres of the country's borders during Durga Puja.

He said BGB personnel have already visited the mandaps and contacted puja committees in their respective areas to coordinate security measures.
“Risks of different kinds can arise at any time. We are collecting intelligence, receiving information from various agencies and working to ensure comprehensive security so that the celebrations can take place without disruption,” the BGB chief said.
He said the force will also ensure security at puja mandaps located within a few kilometres of its headquarters in Pilkhana and other battalion, sector and regional headquarters outside border areas, in coordination with police and other law enforcement agencies.
Ashrafuzzaman said the BGB regularly coordinates with the authorities of the Ramna Kali Mandir, Dhakeshwari National Temple and other nearby puja mandaps in the capital.
He said a 24/7 control room has been opened at BGB headquarters to maintain communication with puja mandaps.
The BGB director general added that the “Sharadiya Surokkha App”, developed under the Ministry of Home Affairs, will allow puja committee members and Ansar personnel deployed at the mandaps to contact law enforcement agencies in case of any problem or emergency.
The BGB will take prompt measures as necessary to maintain security and ensure peaceful and festive celebrations, he said.
Ashrafuzzaman also said intelligence gathering, risk assessment and security measures have been strengthened in coordination with intelligence agencies.
During the visit, he exchanged views with the president and other members of the Ramna Kali Mandir Sarbojonin Puja Udjapan Committee and conveyed his greetings to members of the Hindu community on the occasion of Durga Puja.
Other senior BGB officials were present during the inspection.

item.title: Bangladesh ranks 84th in Global Hunger Index 2026
item.description:
Bangladesh has ranked 84th in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2026, with a score of 19.2, placing the country in the “moderate” hunger category.
The index assesses hunger and undernutrition using four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and under-five mortality.
Bangladesh ranked ahead of India and Pakistan but behind Nepal in the index, which assesses hunger and undernutrition across countries.
India ranked 100th with a score of 24.1 while Pakistan stood at 106th with a score of 25.5. Both countries fell into the “serious” hunger category, according to the report.
Nepal ranked 72nd with a score of 14.5, placing it in the “moderate” category.
A lower GHI score indicates a lower level of hunger, while rankings reflect countries’ relative positions among those included in the assessment.
The Global Hunger Index is published annually by Concern Worldwide, Welthungerhilfe and the Institute for International Law of Peace and Armed Conflict (IFHV) to track hunger and undernutrition worldwide.
The 2026 report warns that global hunger is rising again, with conflicts, climate shocks and economic crises threatening food security.
In Bangladesh, 8.2% of the population is undernourished, while 24% of children under five suffer from stunting, or low height for their age.
The report also shows that 12.9% of children under five suffer from wasting, or low weight for their height, while 3% of children die before reaching their fifth birthday.
Bangladesh has made progress in reducing child stunting over the past two decades.
The proportion of children under five affected by stunting fell from 54.9% in 2000 to 24% in the latest assessment, a reduction of 30.9% points.
Under the GHI classification, scores below 10 indicate low hunger, scores from 10 to 19.9 indicate moderate hunger, scores from 20 to 34.9 indicate serious hunger, scores from 35 to 49.9 indicate alarming hunger, and scores of 50 or above indicate extremely alarming hunger.
The Global Hunger Index is published annually by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe to measure and track hunger and undernutrition worldwide.
According to the index, a lower score indicates a lower level of hunger, while a country’s ranking depends on its position relative to other countries included in the assessment.

item.title: PM calls Dhaka’s air pollution a matter of shame
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday urged people from all walks of life to come forward to protect the environment and forests, calling Dhaka’s persistent air pollution a matter of shame for the country.
Speaking at a meeting to review the progress and implementation of activities of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, he also stressed the need for greater public awareness and collective efforts to build a liveable Bangladesh for future generations.
The prime minister urged government officials to take initiatives beyond their assigned duties to protect the environment and forests.
The meeting, held at the ministry’s conference room, decided to identify and preserve the country’s mother trees within the next six months.
It also directed the authorities to ensure regular care of planted trees, monitor their survival through field visits, and explore ways to expand afforestation in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
Noting that people have limited access to places where they can spend time in nature, Tarique Rahman stressed the need to increase such spaces and encourage people to develop rooftop and school gardens, as well as gardens in different buildings.
He said public awareness is essential alongside government initiatives to protect the environment, adding that greater awareness will make the work easier.
The prime minister also stressed the need for separate public awareness plans to support the implementation of decisions and programmes for environmental and forest conservation.
Expressing concern over Dhaka’s air pollution, he said the capital has been ranking first or second among the world’s most polluted cities for many years.
“This is a matter of shame for the country. Everyone must take responsibility from their respective positions to change the situation,” Tarique Rahman said.
Addressing ministry officials, he said they have the capacity to do more than their assigned duties.
“Your capacity goes a little beyond the duties assigned to you,” the prime minister said, urging officials not to stop at performing their routine responsibilities but to make further efforts for the country and its people.
He said not everyone gets the opportunity to work for the country, and those in responsible positions should make the most of it.
“Allah has given us an opportunity to do something for this country and its people. You may work from nine to five [9am-5pm]. Nobody will say anything if you do nothing beyond that. But if the environment deteriorates, future generations will suffer, because your next generation will also live in this country,” Tarique Rahman said.
He said everyone needs to go beyond their formal responsibilities and contribute more to keeping the environment healthy.
Those seeking change, the prime minister added, should use their abilities and come forward.
Referring to the plan to plant 250 million trees, he said the entire population will benefit if the programme is implemented properly. Collective efforts, he added, could bring positive results for the people.
The meeting also decided that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change will take initiatives to make up for any shortfall if other ministries fail to meet their tree-planting targets.
Regular maintenance and monitoring of planted trees will also be ensured.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo, State Minister Shaikh Faridul Islam, Prime Minister’s Special Assistant Dr Md Saimum Parvez, acting Secretary Fahmida Khanom and senior officials attended the meeting.

item.title: Dengue claims 10 lives in a day, highest toll yet again
item.description:
Ten people died of dengue in Bangladesh in the 24 hours to Thursday morning, matching the highest single-day death toll from the mosquito-borne disease this year, while 1,943 new cases were reported.
The latest fatalities have raised the country’s dengue death toll to 331 this year, while the new cases have taken the total number of infections to 107,259, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the deaths, four were reported in Dhaka South City Corporation area, three in Dhaka North City Corporation area, two in Chittagong division and one was recorded in Dhaka division, it said.
Earlier, on October 6, the country recorded 10 dengue deaths.
Since January 1, hospitals across the country have admitted 107,259 dengue patients. Of them, 101,031 have recovered.

item.title: Govt plans AI-based cancer screening at upazila level
item.description:
The government plans to introduce artificial intelligence (AI)-based screening and testing for breast and cervical cancer at the upazila level to improve access to early detection for women, Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain has said.
He made the remarks while addressing a workshop titled “National Health Protection Authority in Bangladesh: Design and Structural Aspects” as the chief guest at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka on Thursday. The Health Economics Unit of the Health Services Division organized the workshop.
Speaking about women's healthcare, the minister said steps must be taken to ensure that mothers and women do not face embarrassing situations or harassment during pregnancy. To this end, plans are underway to transform health centers into one-stop service centers.
He said the centers would offer AI-based screening and testing for breast and cervical cancer. The government plans to introduce these services at the upazila level in phases and at a low cost.
The initiative is intended to make screening and testing more accessible to women at the upazila level, potentially reducing the need to travel to distant hospitals and making the services more affordable. However, the actual benefits will depend on implementation, service availability and costs.
The minister said primary healthcare was being given the highest priority to bring health services to people's doorsteps. The government has drawn up extensive plans to ensure healthcare for the population, but implementing all the plans at once would be difficult.
He said initiatives were being taken to prioritize activities and introduce them gradually through pilot programs.
The minister also stressed the need to expedite implementation of the Health Protection Act and related activities. Necessary steps were being taken by reviewing and coordinating laws from different countries, he said, adding that special emphasis was being placed on health insurance.
Noting that people have to pay substantial amounts out of their own pockets to cover medical expenses, the minister said this placed them under considerable financial strain.
Calling for coordinated efforts with honesty and dedication to address longstanding irregularities and challenges in the health sector, he said the government was committed to gradually delivering improved and quality healthcare at every level across the country.
Director General of the Health Economics Unit Dr Md Enamul Haque and officials from various divisions of the ministry were present at the workshop.

item.title: Faqir Mahbub: Attempt underway to add 300MW from Rooppur plant to national grid by Nov

"We are making all-out efforts to supply nearly 300MW of electricity from the first reactor of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant to the national grid by this coming November. In addition, we plan to load nuclear fuel into the second reactor around June next year," said the minister.
Underlining the priority attached to the project, Minister Anam noted that as the 1,200MW capacity mega project is a flagship initiative of Russia's state atomic energy corporation, Rosatom, the Russian side is giving it top priority. Teams of experts sent three months ago are working round the clock to meet the project targets.
